o: Do NOT recognise — internally generated brands are prohibited
questions.why: Ind AS 38 bars recognition of internally generated brands, mastheads and customer lists even if cost is measurable — they cannot be distinguished from the business as a whole.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).

mem.tip: the brand prohibition is an evergreen You can build a name; you cannot book it from inside the house.

questions.stem: Zenith Ltd faces four year-end items: (a) an internally developed brand (cost Rs 40 crore, reliably measurable); (b) litigation inflow of Rs 80 crore assessed probable but not virtually certain; (c) loyalty points redeemable for free goods (value Rs 30 crore); (d) a Rs 5 crore item immaterial alone but one of 12 identical items.

o: Disclosed as contingent asset; recognised only when inflow is virtually certain
questions.why: Contingent assets: probable ⇒ disclose; virtually certain ⇒ recognise. The asymmetry vs provisions (probable ⇒ book) is deliberate conservatism.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: probable vs virtually-certain asymmetry is the crux Losses book early; gains knock twice before entering.

o: A material right — deferred revenue recognised on redemption/expiry
questions.why: Under Ind AS 115, options that give a material right not available without the contract ⇒ allocate its standalone value and defer; recognise when points are redeemed or expire.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

mem.tip: material-right identification drives the answer Free future goods are sold today — deferred until used or forgotten.

questions.q: Had (b) been merely possible (not probable), it would be:
o: Disclose only, unless remote — then nothing
questions.why: Possible outflow (for a gain: possible inflow) — contingent; disclosure discipline per Ind AS 37 for losses, and for gains recognition only at virtual certainty.

questions.q: Under the Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting, which one is the single pervasive CONSTRAINT on useful financial reporting?
questions.why: Faithful representation, comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability are enhancing qualitative characteristics; the framework lists the cost constraint (and materiality as entity-specific of relevance) as the pervasive constraint. Options A/B/D improve usefulness but are not constraints.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the constraint vs characteristics distinction is the most-tested single line of the Framework Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Constraint test: the Framework has ONE pervasive constraint — cost vs benefit. Materiality is entity-specific to relevance. Sort characteristics into fundamental (relevance+faithful rep) vs enhancing (CRTU) before eliminating options.

questions.q: As per the revised Conceptual Framework, which of the following is NOT a component of 'faithful representation'?
questions.why: Faithful representation = complete, neutral and free from error. Prudence was retained in the 2018 Conceptual Framework as an aspect of neutrality (cautious judgement), not as a separate component of faithful representation.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — framework ingredients are repeatable as 'not / except' questions Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: A faithful trio: Complete, Neutral, Error-free. Prudence lives inside neutrality now — not a fourth pillar.

questions.q: The Conceptual Framework identifies several measurement bases. Which combination is correctly matched?
o: Historical cost — amount paid in cash at acquisition
Current value — only fair value qualifies
Value in use — exit price notion
Fair value — highest and best use for non-financial assets is ignored by Ind AS 113
questions.why: Historical cost is the cash/cash-equivalents paid at recognition. Current value includes fair value, value in use/fulfilment value and current cost; Ind AS 113 uses exit price and considers market participants' highest and best use for non-financial assets.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — measurement-base matching questions recur in Section B of the objective paper AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Bases: HC, FC, VC, PV, VU. Fair value = EXIT price, highest-and-best-use belongs to buyer's view — never the entity's intent.

questions.q: A liability's definition under the Conceptual Framework centres on:
o: Present obligation arising from past events whose settlement is expected to cause an outflow
questions.why: Liability = present obligation (legal or constructive) arising from past events, settlement resulting in outflow of economic resources. 'Probable' features in recognition, not definition.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — definition-vs-recognition wording is a favourite Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Definitions describe; recognition tests gate. Obligations are legal or constructive — both bite.

questions.q: An item meeting the definition of an asset is recognised when:
o: It is material and probable future economic benefits will flow AND it can be measured reliably
questions.why: Recognition criteria: probable future economic benefits + reliable measurement + definition (the Framework's recognition gate).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — gate-test wording appears in 'all except' formats Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Three keys turn the recognition lock: definition, probability, measurement. Materiality decides whether anyone should care.

questions.q: The unit of account under the Framework determines:
o: What rights and obligations are accounted for (the 'what' being recognised)
questions.why: Unit of account = the right or group of rights (and corresponding obligations) on which recognition and derecognition are based — now explicit in the Framework.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the Framework's explicit additions get questions AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Define the unit before you measure anything: rights first, then numbers.

o: Economic benefits — inflows/enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities with equity effects
questions.why: Income = increases in economic benefits during the period via inflows/enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities that increase equity (other than contributions).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — definition-assembly recognition AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Equity climbs without shareholder money? That's income.

questions.q: Which is an ENHANCING (not fundamental) qualitative characteristic?
questions.why: Fundamental = relevance + faithful representation; enhancing = comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the four-plus-two sort AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Two pillars, four upgrades: C-V-T-U decorate the foundation, not carry the roof.

questions.q: Financial statements are prepared on which basis per the Framework and Ind AS 1?
questions.why: The Framework and Ind AS 1 require the accrual basis (except cash flows).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — freebie definition asked fast Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Only the cash-flow statement lives by the bank statement; everything else follows accrual.

questions.q: The new scheme positions the Conceptual Framework as the gap-filling reference. Under Ind AS 8's judgement hierarchy, the FIRST step when no specific Ind AS applies is to:
o: Look at requirements of standards dealing with similar and related issues
questions.why: Ind AS 8 ladder (unchanged rule, newly emphasised placement): (1) standards on similar issues; (2) Framework concepts (definitions, recognition, measurement); then (3) recent pronouncements/other bodies/practice — consistently applied.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — hierarchy order is a crisp 1-marker for a new syllabus AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Climb the ladder top rung first: similar standards, then the Framework, then the neighbours.
